Tsukqiao (Z60)

Scoring-table region: Haless.

In one sentence: Survive between an overlord and the Oni, then use the lies of the Xion dynasty, masks, and Beikling heritage to rebuild Luzhong.

Story: Very high | Mission-tree length: Long (a prelude followed by a dedicated continuation after forming Luzhong) | Mission tree updated in the current local files 2026-07-09, supports v1.37.5.0 | Uniqueness: Very high | Prison factor: High | Early pressure: High | Expansion capacity: High.

Identity and history

Tsukqiao (Z60) is an existing Beikling country in 1444. Its capital is Tiaochi, it follows the Devouring Path, and it is ruled by Youji I of the Xion dynasty. The opening government has the Tiaochi Mandate, Literati, and Religious Society reforms; eunuchs already participate in government. The king is mediocre and cruel, while Queen Fuyuan Jiao is more politically capable. Her relationship with the Xion dynasty is a central axis of the story; later mission outcomes must not be projected back into the 1444 starting situation.

The offline English Wiki traces Xion rule in Tiaochi back to 1197, describing Beikling clans, the Mask of Might, the Jade Tax paid to Jinqiu and administration by eunuchs. The dynasty habitually rewrites records and exaggerates its genealogy. Its claim to inherit an ancient empire is therefore itself a political claim within the story, not grounds to treat every piece of dynastic propaganda as uncontested history. The Wiki also describes Tsukqiao's conquest by Bianfang in 1453; this belongs to that source's historical line, not an inevitable outcome for a player starting in 1444.

Country story and campaign line

Tsukqiao begins by seeking Beikling autonomy while remaining dependent on surrounding powers. The Oni to the west can provide assistance, but that help leaves debt behind. Jinqiu's protection and the Jade Tax place collection and administration in the hands of the eunuchs. Early missions handle these relationships, contact western Beiklings and the Xiongxiap merchant league, and seek freedom through war, trade, and political integration. The queen's death leaves Youji with a question: how can an incapable ruler fulfil her wish to rebuild the Beikling nation? The mission narrative answers with inflated ancestral achievements, seized titles, and rewritten history, making dynastic legitimacy increasingly dependent on lies.

After independence, the missions expand from the revival of a mountain city to Beikling kin, the powers of Yanshen, and the heritage of old Luzhong. This “imperial restoration” is an alternative future pursued by the player after completing missions. A Beikling Devouring Path country can form Luzhong (V23) through the generic decision. The decision requires a non-tribal, independent or tributary status, specified provinces, and Beikling-culture territory. The continuation checks that the country was once Z60 and is now V23, making it part of the same campaign chain; other eligible Beikling countries can also form V23, but they do not automatically receive the Xion-dynasty prelude.

Core mechanisms

  1. Legitimacy and the Seat of Lies: The formed Xion-dynasty route receives a dedicated government reform and modifiers related to Power and Justice. They strengthen dynastic rule while turning legitimacy into continuing pressure; modifier decay and reform choices are tied to the Broken Lies disaster. The more the state relies on fabricated achievements, the more it must pay to maintain them.
  2. Devouring Path masks and Oni debt: Several Devouring Path church features are already unlocked at the start. Missions can exchange with Oni for money or troops, but the bargain creates long-term debt; later progress requires funds, spy networks, and military strength to repay it. Masks and religious power continue to support armies, titles, and the dynastic narrative.
  3. Eunuch government and mountain restoration: The Tiaochi eunuchs initially assist taxation. After independence, missions can reorganize estates and reform eunuch responsibilities. Forts, workshops, and relic restoration in the Beikling mountains connect construction to military revival, while administrative resources and territorial control remain gates.
  4. Seizing titles and expanding across regions: The missions demand more than land. They also require dealing with Beikling kin, merchant leagues, monasteries, and Haless-wide power. The dynasty uses documents and ritual to explain new conquests as ancient rights, then pursues Luzhong titles and wider imperial claims.

Phased play

Stabilize finances and manpower first, use any available aid to handle the independence war, and prevent Oni debt from becoming a permanent burden. The terrain around the capital favors defense, but mission progress requires actively seeking allies, Beikling land, and trade routes. After independence, eunuchs, estates, religious power, and reform proceed together; repeated warfare alone will not advance the campaign. Forming Luzhong requires the generic decision's territorial and institutional conditions. In the later phase, invest in mountain relics, monasteries, and larger wars across Haless.

The difficulty is the combination of early subject and war pressure with the later cost of maintaining legitimacy and satisfying several mission lines. The final missions can trigger the Broken Lies disaster. It is the dedicated dynastic-collapse ending, not a claim that recovery afterward or any single outcome is inevitable history.

Formation and ending

Tsukqiao is the starting country Z60; Luzhong is the formable V23. Beikling Devouring Path countries form Luzhong through a generic decision and its follow-up events, while the former-Z60 condition preserves the Xion-dynasty continuation. The late missions rebuild old Luzhong, seize titles, restore relics, and unite the Beiklings through an imperial myth; the final mission also plants the crisis of that myth's collapse. The player can complete the imperial project, but the tree does not present Xion rule as a victory without cost.

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 92/100 | Authoritarianism 91/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 78/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 74/100) | Pluralism 39/100. Phase change: Tsukqiao_early (Expansion 68, Authoritarianism 66) → Luzhong_late (Expansion 95, Authoritarianism 94). The country moves from mountain survival to cross-regional expansion, centralizing power through dynasty, eunuchs, and religious masks. Ritual is a political tool, while the later route increasingly demands Beikling identity and Devouring Path order.

The v2.1 value is Neutral (38/100), with a deteriorating trajectory. Phase change: Tsukqiao_liberation (Neutral 60/100) → Luzhong_dynastic_empire (Neutral 38/100). Freeing Beiklings from external rule and rebuilding cities have public benefits. Extraction from subjects, rule by fear, and institutionalized deception harm dignity and restraint. Expansion and centralization are not counted as evil by themselves.

Recommended for players who enjoy character-driven stories, restoration ambitions, religious masks, and crisis management. If you do not want to maintain fragile legitimacy after the opening war, or dislike late territorial, title, and relic requirements, this long campaign will be punishing.

Community experience

Two June 2026 post-update experiences praised the Beikling restoration and its unique disaster. One found the legitimacy system interesting but expected late event waiting; another liked the wonder construction and the climax against the Command. Neither identified an exact patch number. They describe player experience at that time only and do not replace current scripts or hands-on verification.

Evidence boundary

Tag, localised names, formation relations, and mission conditions follow the current local Mod and localisation. The Wiki evidence supports the bounded historical claims above, but does not establish every mission mechanic or the exact player experience. The 2026 official development diary is evidence of design intent at that date; no usable Chinese offline Wiki page was found. The article keeps the distinction between starting facts, conditional formation, and later mission future. Any intermediate borders from the Halann historical map remain community reconstruction; dynastic genealogy, some dates, and exact late-game experience remain source-bounded. See the original source evidence and the additional English receipt.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces the current local national-idea text and script effects. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock in order, and the ambition applies after all seven. This lists national ideas only, excluding racial, government, and mission rewards. Conditional or alternative sets are shown separately and are not treated as simultaneous. An idea description may recall history or describe a future ideal; it does not by itself establish that the event had already occurred in 1444.

Tsukqiao (Z60) — Tsukqiao Ideas

Traditions: Tsukqiao Traditions

Effects: Land morale recovery speed: +15%; Looting speed: +25%.

Idea 1: Sons of the Mist Hills

In the west of Yanshen there lies a mountain range that goes by many names, but its people know it as the Black Mist Hills, a colossal labyrinth of mountains and valleys that stretches along almost the entire northwestern border of Yanshen. It has been the source of many legends told by outsiders who look upon these hills and see the mystical veil of fog that adorns them. But to the Beiklings they have become home, for centuries they have inhabited these hills and have learned to traverse the many mountains and ravines that are hidden within the mist. To the people that have chosen to live in this land it is a natural bastion and the greatest advantage the Beiklings have against any foreign force seeking their demise.

Effect: Fort defense: +15%.

Idea 2: The Jade Tax

Tsukqiao has been a subject of the Eternal Council for almost 100 years now, and although this has allowed them to survive, it also came with a cost. Their overlords demand their tribute, the so-called 'Jade Tax' in reference to the Shirgrii serving as the seat of the council. To be able to afford said tribute the rulers of Tsukqiao have to spend a great deal of time moving around their lands, collecting taxes from every subject as well as the raiders using their lands as a secure base. It is thus not rare to see the members of the dynasty roaming around the hills and valleys, visiting every settlement in an effort to meet the quota. This has over the years allowed Tsukqiao to pay the onerous tribute and even produce a surplus big enough to fund the activities of their rulers.

Effect: National tax modifier: +15%.

Idea 3: Teachings in the Dark

Our history with the Devouring Path is a long one. Since the day the Black King donned the Mask of Many Faces for the first time we as a people have been connected to the dark arts in many ways. We have learned and made use of many sinister techniques that have allowed our people to dominate Yanshen in times long gone, but little compares to one of our most infamous techniques. Through the infusion of chi during a ritual, one is able to create masks with the ability to alter the enemy’s perception of themselves and provide the wearer with enhanced perception and combat skills, some warriors even claim their masks would speak to them and offer them guidance in battle. Our time of domination is but a distant shadowy memory, but this technique survives amongst the people of Tsukqiao, and it continues to give us an advantage when fighting our enemies once more.

Effect: Shock damage: +10%.

Idea 4: Lessons from the Oni

One cannot follow the Devouring Path without feeling the influence of the Oni, they have molded and perfected the arts of the forbidden path, and ever since the Path has risen in popularity amongst the human inhabitants of the hills their ways of thinking have come as part of the teachings. But not all techniques the demons of the hills teach are of a destructive nature, the devouring path opens many doors to prohibited knowledge, some of which may give us an advantage if we seek to reform Tsukqiao away from its most dysfunctional aspects. Whatever uttered word of power or scraps of proscribed writing can help us learn new ways and give us an advantage against the people of the lowlands, far wealthier and more established than our mountain realm, is worth the price.

Effect: Technology cost: -5%.

Idea 5: In the Shadows of the Giants

The Beikling homeland once was one lit up by myriad fires. Across the hillside many forges would ceaselessly produce the weapons and armors for the raiders of the Terror Empire to use on their campaigns of pillaging. Little remains of those times, most of the greatest forges of the land have long been destroyed or fallen into disuse, plunging the land into shadows. But some remain and continue to see use by locals who keep the long lasting memory of the forgemasters of yore alive. Tiaochi possesses one of the most notorious forges of the current era, which takes the ore mined from the mountain depths and molds them into weapons for our armies and raiders.

Effects: Army attrition: -10%; Army maintenance modifier: -10%.

Idea 6: Cult of Xion

The history of the Xion dynasty is difficult to study, for there are very few accounts about their origins or history, and what is there to be found is … hard to believe. As the official story goes, it was Jiefu Xion who founded Tsukqiao after the fall of the Jaherian administration; he was the grandson of a governor from Lanqiu and his father was a general stationed at the local garrison. The story then goes on to claim that he was a descendant from the last king of the old empire, claiming that the last member of the Fei dynasty did in fact survive after the fall of their dynasty and his family would come to be known as the Xion. It was supposedly Jiefu himself who, after finding the Mask of Might, received a revelation about his royal origins from the mask.

This tale strains the credulity of most people, but to the members of the Xion Dynasty it is a truth as real as the mountains they rule over. They honor Jiefu as a great conqueror who brought unity in a time of division and they believe it is their birthright to reunite the Mask of Many Faces and proclaim a new Beikling empire.

Effects: Legitimacy: +1; Devotion: +1; Horde unity: +1; Republican tradition: +0.3; Prestige: +1.

Idea 7: Legacy of Great Luzhong

Long before the tigerfolk stalked into Yanshen, we were united under the empire of Great Luzhong, a mighty realm that ravaged much of the Yanhe river lands, striking terror with masked raiders and armies fueled by the grand forges that gleamed all over the misty hills, razing countless settlements to the ground and abducting their inhabitants to serve as fuel for dark rituals, all to serve the great rulers who wore the Mask of Many Faces, a symbol of our immense power and glory. This glorious era ultimately came to an end, when a broken and leaderless Luzhong fell to the invasion of Harimar, their warriors destroying our cities and establishing strongholds to ensure we would forever stay beneath their heel.

Now, with Harimar long dead, Yanshen fractured and all the fragments of the great mask once more in possession of our people, it is time for the Terror Empire to rise again.

Effect: Core-creation cost: -10%.

Ambition: Tsukqiao Ambition

Effect: Harsh treatment cost: -25%.

Luzhong (V23) — Luzhong Ideas

Traditions: Luzhong Traditions

Effects: Fort defense: +20%; Ruler's same-faith advisor cost: -10%.

Idea 1: Divided Nevermore

It has been too long since a Beikling state held power. Too long since a Beikling was respected and feared across the land; too long since we Beiklings had a realm that could rule and exert law even outside our borders, one that we could truly be proud of.

It has been too long since Luzhong fell to Harimar.

For years we have lived under the boot of foreign kings, ruled by external powers and divided across our land. The only time we managed to rise was under the rule of an unworthy dynasty of weak cowards, just for us to fall in turn to a new conqueror from lands far beyond.

No more.

The Masks have been reforged, our people have been reunited, the banners of the empire fly proud over the mountains of our homeland.

For the first time in fifteen hundred years, the great title has been claimed by someone worthy, one destined to be ruler of all Beiklings.

Let it be known; we will not fail again.

Effect: Shock damage: +15%.

Idea 2: To Rule the Hills

The Mist Hills of Yanshen are a beast of their own, the source of many tales and horror stories due to their almost ethereal nature. Many people have died trying to navigate their treacherous terrain or from getting lost in their labyrinthine passes, but to us the Hills are a safe haven, a homeland far away from the grasp of the withering warmongers of the south.

To these lesser realms, our region is almost impossible to rule; our people have a long history of fighting off interlopers, keeping them at bay and only submitting under favorable terms. It's from these heights that our people launch our infamous raids, keeping the traditions of old alive.

With the return of the Empire, we can now begin to reclaim our rightful rule of the hills that saw our birth, extending our authority to the many autonomous communities that live in the valleys at their flank. Our people bow to their rightful ruler with pride, knowing the broken title has a new claimant after millennia.

The beast does not bow, but it can be taught not to bite the hand it feeds it.

Effect: global_autonomy: -0.1%.

Idea 3: Yaoren

The Yan of the lowlands call us 'Yaoren', the Demon Men. For hundreds of years we were their greatest fear - our warriors ravaged and pillaged much of the land, carrying away untold riches and leaving despair and devastation in their wake. We fed their captured peasants to the rituals of our Empire, granting our armies untold powers to continue this deadly cycle.

Even after the fall of the great realm, our people continued to live up to the Yaoren title, terrorising the Yan people and leaving them in constant dread of our raids.

With the return of the Empire, we can once more organize great raider hosts of the kind the old kings used to command. With them, we will remind the Yanshen exactly how we earned our nickname.

Effects: Religious power modifier: +20%; Looting speed: +50%.

Idea 4: The Mask of Many Faces

Many years ago, in a period almost lost to history, there was an exchange that would seal our destiny forever.

A delegate Oni was sent down the mountains to make an offer to the then Fei King of Old Luzhong, a realm that up to that point was just another follower of the common folklore of Haless.

The Oni brought with him a tribute, a mask like no other. Composed of 4 smaller masks bound by a central gem, the Mask of Many Faces was a sight to be beholden. It enraptured our ruler, who refused to take the mask off, and in the span of a year he would come to wither away. His son, who would come to be known as 'The Red King Fei', wore the mask to his enthronement, rejecting the old ceremonial one used until then. He would come to be the first Devouring Path King of Luzhong, beginning our people’s long association with the dark arts.

The original meaning of each Mask has been lost for many years, but as we understand it today they are: Might, the power to rule. Wealth, a sign of prosperity. Control, of oneself and of others. And Right, to sit on the throne and wear the mask.

These are the virtues of the Beikling People, and we will inflict the terror of a thousand deaths on our enemies if it means protecting the union.

Effect: Morale damage: +10%.

Idea 5: The Might of the Land

Deep beneath the mountains of Yanshen, there is a power that awaits control. To we Beiklings, it is as vital to life as food or water, and it is central to the functioning of our society. It played a key role in giving us an advantage in battle in times past, and to this day remains the reason why our raiders are as fearful and dangerous as they are. That power is ore.

The Mist Hills are home to some of the biggest veins of metals in Haless. In the past we learned to use these metals to forge the weapons of war our warriors used to fight our enemies; at our height, the hillsides of the Beikling homeland resembled the night sky, lit by hundreds of forges that produced all the goods our armies and raiders needed. Amongst these, the forge of Yinsheng was the very greatest, standing as the beacon of Luzhong’s power and responsible for many innovations in the creation of weaponry.

Long years have passed since this era of light came to an end, and darkness has enveloped the Mist Hills, but with the return of the Empire this era must be reborn too. The rekindled fires of a thousand forges shall brighten our path to absolute power once more, the might of our homeland reforged from the ashes of what once was.

Effects: Goods produced modifier: +10%; Prestige: +1.

Idea 6: Sheng Shan

The Sheng Shan are the holiest mounds in our lands; each is crowned by an isolated monastery, the remote location of which is intended to bring the monks to closer contact with the spirits that flit around our homeland. We commune with forces seen as taboo by the rest of Yanshen there, bury our dead so they may join them upon their peaks, and perform dark rites within the temples.

The first Sheng Shan was built by the Oni as a tomb for the Red King. They became iconic of the early and middle Imperial Era of Luzhong as great centers of religion amongst the common folk. The most famous of them and one of the few that remains is the temple of Chatzin. A place deemed of great spiritual connection amongst those who follow the dark teachings, it was the home of some of the most brutal rituals done during this time.

Even in the present we continue to build Sheng Shan mounds, and taking care of them is a matter of prestige for the communities that live nearby.

Effect: Missionary strength: +2%.

Idea 7: Empire Evermore

Luzhong is again, Luzhong shall be forever.

The realm shall not break again; no external power shall rule the Beiklings anymore.

We will not allow it.

We have been reforged, rebirthed from the hatred of a people who have cried one too many tears over the world who is choosing to forget they even exist.

Our state, our Empire of Terror, shall be the one to rule - and we will do so with an iron fist, one of retribution and vengeance.

They shall know dread like their ancestors did. They shall tremble when hearing of our arrival. They shall live in terror just as we did all the long centuries after our fall.

They shall learn to fear our name once more.

Eternal and evermore, Luzhong will not fall again.

Effect: Core-creation cost: -15%.

Ambition: Luzhong Ambition

Effect: Maximum absolutism: +15%.
